body.statement: Apply CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), to the marks \(Y/2\) and multiply its clipped output by two. For \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), the resulting banked real-mark heavy-light estimator admits the four-coordinate representation in \(def:four-coordinate-lift-handle\), is computable using \(O(dL_n^3)\) arithmetic operations, and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\widehat T_{\mathrm L}-\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})]|\lesssim_{\epsilon}Md/[n\log(en)]\); its pilot misclassification contribution has the same order. The representation preserves the banked factorial coefficients, zero fallbacks, clipping, and expectation identities and exposes the selected marked-factorial statistic required by \(def:direct-calibration-handle\).
body.justification: This compatibility lemma imports the established real-mark heavy-light approximation and verifies exactly the representation needed by the new observable tail score; it is not an independent approximation novelty claim.
body.gap: CausalSmithHeterogeneityFrontier2026, \(thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution\), already supplies the clipped real-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator and its risk order. The remaining bridge is to expose its pilot-selected light statistic in a form on which the data-only tail calibration can act without changing the banked expectation and bias guarantees.
body.consumer: The bias half of the globally honest upper interval and the rare-cell contribution in the \(n=9915,d=8196\) 401(k) analysis.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(L:=\log(en)\), and apply
\(\mathtt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_heterogeneity\_frontier}/\mathtt{thm:robust\text{-}upper\text{-}construction\text{-}resolution}\)
to the outcome \(\widetilde Y:=Y/2\).  This application is legitimate for every
\(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).  Indeed,
\[
 |E_P[\widetilde Y\mid A=a,X=k]|=|\mu_{ak}|/2\le M/2
\]
by \(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\), and Lyapunov's elementary moment
inequality, proved here by Cauchy--Schwarz, gives
\[
 E_P[(\widetilde Y-\mu_{ak}/2)^2\mid A=a,X=k]
 \le \{E_P[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid A=a,X=k]\}^{1/2}/4
 \le M^2/4.
\tag{1}
\]
The source model's heterogeneity parameter can be set to \(2\), since the
scaled conditional effects and their average both lie in \([-M,M]\).  Fixed
overlap is exactly \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\), and the sample split remains
independent by \(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\).

We spell out the algebra that turns the imported one-mark lift into the four
coordinates in the present core.  Write
\[
 x_0=p_k(1-\pi_k),\qquad x_1=p_k\pi_k,\qquad
 z_a=x_a\mu_{ak},\qquad p_k=x_0+x_1.
\tag{2}
\]
The calibrated source construction takes
\[
 K=\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor,\quad
 \alpha_0=\min\{1,(64\log6)^{-1},(512D_6)^{-1}\},
 \quad D_6=8\log(27/4),
\]
and \(B=4096L/m_1\), where \(m_1\) is the size of its estimation fold; its
pilot threshold is \(256L\).  Select \(c_L=\alpha_0\).  Then \(K\le L_n\),
and all source polynomials belong to the larger space \(\mathscr Q_{L_n}\).
For the shifted Chebyshev polynomial \(T_K\), define, with continuous values at
zero,
\[
 H_K(t)=\frac{1-T_K(1-2t)}{2K^2},\qquad
 E_K(t)=\frac{H_K(t)}t,\qquad
 G_K(t)=\frac{1-E_K(t)}t.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(T_K(\cos\vartheta)=\cos(K\vartheta)\),
\[
 0\le t\{1-tG_K(t)\}=H_K(t)\le K^{-2},
 \qquad 0\le t\le1.
\tag{4}
\]
Moreover \(G_K\) has degree at most \(K-2\).  Consequently
\[
 q_a(x_0,x_1):=\frac{x_0+x_1}{B}G_K(x_a/B)
\]
has degree at most \(K-1\le L_n-1\), and
\[
 (x_0,z_0,x_1,z_1)\longmapsto z_1q_1(x_0,x_1)-z_0q_0(x_0,x_1)
 \in\mathscr Q_{L_n}.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus (5) is precisely the four-coordinate representation claimed in
\(def:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}lift\text{-}handle\).

For completeness, consider any selected light cell on the pilot-good event,
so that \(p_k\le B/4\).  By overlap, \(x_a\ge\epsilon p_k\).  Equations
(2)--(4), \(|\mu_{ak}|\le M\), and \(x_a/B\in[0,1]\) imply
\[
 \left|p_k\mu_{ak}-\frac{p_kz_a}{B}G_K(x_a/B)\right|
 =p_k|\mu_{ak}|\frac{H_K(x_a/B)}{x_a/B}
 \le \frac{MB}{\epsilon K^2}.
\tag{6}
\]
The ordered distinct-index falling-factorial statistic carrying one outcome
mark is unbiased for every monomial \(z_ap_kx_a^j\): expanding its expectation
as a sum over distinct indices and using independence gives the product of the
corresponding one-observation expectations.  Hence linearity and (6), first
conditionally on the pilot and then unconditionally, yield
\[
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}-
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
 \right]\right|
 \le \frac{2MdB}{\epsilon K^2}+\mathcal E_{\mathrm{pilot}}.
\tag{7}
\]
The binomial Chernoff calculation contained in the imported construction gives
for its pilot-good event \(\mathcal A\))
\[
 Q_P^{(n)}(\mathcal A^c)\le 2d\exp(-c\,256L)\le Cn^{-6}
\tag{8}
\]
after reducing \(c_\epsilon\) if necessary.  The same construction's explicit
coefficient bound \(6^{2K}\le n^{1/32}\), together with its factorial second
moment identity and (1), gives by Cauchy--Schwarz
\(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{pilot}}\le C_\epsilon Mn^{-2}\).  This is at most
\(C_\epsilon Md/(nL)\) after enlarging the constant over the finitely many
small values of \(n\).  Since \(m_1\asymp n\), \(B\asymp L/n\), and
\(K\asymp L\), (7) becomes
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}
 \left|E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
 \widehat T_{\mathrm L}-
 \sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})
 \right]\right|
 \le C_\epsilon M\frac{d}{n\log(en)}.
\tag{9}
\]
Equation (8) proves the asserted pilot-misclassification order as well.
Finally, the coefficient recurrence has \(O(L_n^2)\) coefficients, and the
four-coordinate bookkeeping and pilot split add at most a factor \(L_n\), so
the imported \(O(dL_n^2)\) implementation is, in particular,
\(O(dL_n^3)\).  Rescaling the marks by one half and multiplying the output by
two preserves every expectation identity, zero fallback, and clipping rule.
